note: Brazil is the best-documented tradition in this table at muscle level, and the reason is the export trade: ABIEC's bilingual Livro Brasileiro de Cortes Bovinos gives, for nearly every commercial cut, a "Componentes musculares" line in Portuguese and a "Base óssea" line naming the bones the cut is taken off - a muscle list and a boundary, per cut, out of one document. It is an industry association book rather than a government specification, so everything resting on it is graded `trade`, never `standard`. Fetching it needs a note for whoever comes next: the PDF is 18 MB, over the WebFetch size limit, and has to be pulled with curl and read with pdftotext; every quote here was re-extracted a page at a time and string-matched against the PDF before being written down. Two things the book does not cover: the cuts that stay bone-in and domestic (costela, ponta de agulha) have labelled anatomical plates but no cut entry, and matambre has neither, so its muscle naming comes from the Argentine and Uruguayan trade instead. ABIEC's English column is a rough translation and renders "grande dorsal" (latissimus dorsi) as "rectus capiti dorsalis major" in two places; the Portuguese is what is quoted. Every quote in this file was checked against a local copy of its page before being written: the ABIEC ones against a reading-order pdftotext dump of the PDF, the BeefPoint, argentinebeef.org.ar, delsurbeef.com and carnenossa ones against curl'd HTML, and the Calkins ones against calkins-table.md in this folder. All 73 matched verbatim. This matters because WebFetch answers are written by a summarising model that paraphrases and merges adjacent sentences, so nothing that came back through it alone was trusted as a quote.

cuts.dispute: Two different things are called an "aba" and no source reconciles them. (A) ABIEC defines the aba do contrafilé (B1112.1) as the flap removed from the striploin, and names it as "músculos intercostais, serrato dorsal caudal e íliocostal" - a rib-end flap, not abdominal wall. (B) Brazilian retail butchery routinely treats "aba de filé" as a synonym of "bife do vazio", which ABIEC (B1210) defines as "a porção grossa do músculo reto abdominal"; that reading matches the atlas's own description of the cut as a sheet of abdominal wall, and is what the region rectangle draws. Both candidates are listed in `muscles`. No Brazilian standard or trade source was found that names muscles under the literal heading "aba de filé", so the grade is contested rather than trade. Bounds are inferred: ABIEC gives bone bases for the contrafilé and for the bife do vazio, not for a cut called aba de filé.

cuts.dispute: Three named candidates, and the split is real rather than an error in one source. (A) rectus abdominis - ABIEC B1210 "Bife do Vazio / Flank Steak": "constituído pela porção grossa do músculo reto abdominal", bone base "bordo distal da última costela, apófises transversas das vértebras lombares e tuberosidade do íleo". The atlas names this cut "Fraldinha (vazio)", so if fraldinha is the vazio, this is it. (B) obliquus internus abdominis - BeefPoint, citing Carnes e Cortes (1999) and the Atlas of Topographical Anatomy of the Domestic Animals (1971), states flatly that the internal oblique is the muscle that takes the name fraldinha. (C) diaphragm, pars costalis - ABIEC's export nomenclature does not use "fraldinha" for any flank cut at all: item B1211 "Fraldinha" is the Thin Skirt / Hampe, "a porção costal do diafragma", and the flank steak is sold as "Bife do Vazio" instead. Candidate C is deliberately left out of `muscles`: it is an export-trade homonym for the outside skirt, which is not where this atlas draws the rectangle. A and B are both kept, and the disagreement between them is the finding. Bounds are ABIEC's, from the Bife do Vazio bone base: last rib to the tuber coxae of the ilium. That line is the same for either abdominal candidate, so bounds are graded trade even though the muscle list is contested.

cuts.dispute: No source names a muscle. ABIEC's variety-meats item 550 defines the tail entirely by bone - "as vértebras coccígeas e músculos correspondentes" - and leaves "músculos correspondentes" unexpanded, exactly as the UK oxtail does in FINDINGS. The assignment to `sacrocaudalis` is inference from anatomy rather than from a source: the sacrocaudal dorsal and ventral groups are what runs along the caudal vertebrae, and the model carries them under one id. Bounds are graded trade because the bone limit is stated - ABIEC's carcass and alcatra specs keep the first two coccygeal vertebrae with the rump, so the tail starts behind them.

sources.quote: A peça é preparada após remoção do osso hióide, gorduras, tecido conjuntivo e gânglios regionais.

cuts.dispute: No source names a muscle, and here that is the right answer rather than a gap. ABIEC's item 510 is a variety-meat spec written entirely in terms of trim - the hyoid bone, fat, connective tissue and lymph nodes come off and the piece is graded by weight or colour - and no Brazilian cut standard describes the tongue's own musculature at all. The atlas models no lingual muscle either: `masseter` and `temporalis` are the jaw, not the tongue, so nothing in `muscles` would be honest. The intrinsic and extrinsic lingual muscles are listed as unmodelled from bovine anatomy so that whoever extends muscle.json has the spec. Bounds are inferred for the same reason: the tongue's limits are the hyoid apparatus and the floor of the mouth, neither of which is a boundary along a modelled muscle.
